scope: rootless bubblewrap user/pid/mount-proc namespace regular-file descriptor visibility and util-linux user namespace UID mapping

descriptor_probe.descriptor_object_type: regular file containing only a synthetic test sentinel
descriptor_probe.effect: same-host-UID process outside bwrap opened /proc/15/fd/9 for a regular file and read the synthetic sentinel bytes

user_namespace_mapping.auto_mapping_stderr: unshare: failed to execute newuidmap: No such file or directory

conclusion: On this host, rootless bwrap PID and proc namespaces did not prevent an external process with the same host UID from reading regular-file descriptor contents through host /proc. This does not demonstrate opening or duplicating a Unix socket descriptor, stealing a Unix socket endpoint, or ptrace/process-memory access; none was tested. unshare --map-root-user maps namespace root to the same host UID; subordinate ranges are configured but auto mapping fails because newuidmap is absent. No distinct host UID identity was demonstrated.
limits: This is local evidence from one Linux environment, not adversarial validation.
It does not test SELinux/AppArmor, a different host UID, or a production launcher.
The descriptor was a regular file; no Unix socket FD duplication, socket endpoint theft, ptrace, or process-memory read was tested.
The sentinel file and sandbox process were removed after the probe.
